julia: Hey team — hitting 401 invalid_api_key from hosted API only in our prod edge function. Local curl + Postman work fine. Happening ~10% of requests, same key. Any ideas?

maya: Sorry you're seeing that. Quick Qs: is the key definitely the same one used locally? Any proxies or middleware in that function?

julia: Yep same env var. We fetch from a lambda@edge-like container (edge runtime). No external proxies. We log the outgoing request headers and sometimes Authorization header is missing entirely. Example attach: we set header in code then call fetch.

julia: Repro snippet that fails intermittently in prod runtime:
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hi'})
});
console.log('sent-auth', process.env.RW_API_KEY ? 'present' : 'missing');
```

julia: Logs show: `sent-auth present` but the outgoing dump from our runtime shows no Authorization header for the failing requests. curl from the same host with the same key works.

ben: Hmm interesting. Is anything instrumenting or monkey-patching fetch in that runtime? Some APM/perf libs wrap fetch and sometimes mutate/replace request objects.

julia: We do have a perf agent: `perf-agent` (v2.0.0) loaded via `NODE_OPTIONS=--require /opt/perf/agent.js` for metrics. We didn't suspect it but we'll try disabling it.

maya: If that consistently repros when the agent is loaded, it's likely the wrapper strips headers for cross-origin calls (some agents do that for privacy). Can you try temporarily starting the function without the agent and reproducing?

julia: Just tested — disabled NODE_OPTIONS and the failure rate goes to 0 in a 200 req run. With agent enabled ~11 failures out of 200. Agent seems to be the culprit.

ben: Thanks for confirming. Do you have the agent source or a small stacktrace? Common bug: the agent replaces globalThis.fetch with a wrapper that builds a new Request but forgets to copy `headers` when the original request used a Headers object.

julia: I pulled the agent code — it wraps like: `globalThis.fetch = (url, opts) => { const newReq = new Request(url, opts); /* measure */ return originalFetch(newReq); }` — I see it constructs Request from opts but doesn't preserve the Authorization header if opts.headers is a Headers instance; it loses some header cases intermittently.

ryan: That explains it. Request constructor behavior depends on how headers are passed. If opts.headers is a Headers object and later mutated or non-enumerable, copying can drop values. Workarounds: (1) update agent to preserve headers explicitly (`new Headers(opts.headers)`), (2) set Authorization as a string-keyed plain object before fetch, or (3) avoid preloading agent via NODE_OPTIONS and require it after setting global fetch.

julia: Quick workaround: changed code to pass headers as plain object: `{ Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}` }` (we already did) — but agent still loses some. We updated perf-agent locally to use `const hdrs = new Headers(); for (const [k,v] of new Headers(opts.headers || {})) hdrs.set(k, v); const newReq = new Request(url, { ...opts, headers: hdrs });` and failures stopped.

maya: Great. For short-term help, you can also add a retry on 401 with a one-off log that dumps raw outgoing headers (careful with secrets) to confirm. For a permanent fix we should get perf-agent patched and rolled.

julia: Filing internal ticket to update perf-agent to v2.0.1 with header-preserve fix. Can support escalate if you want to block a rollout.

ben: We'll follow up with the perf team. Also leaving a note: when a client sees `401 invalid_api_key` but curl/postman succeed, check for header rewriting/middleware, global polyfills, and things that serialize/deserialize Headers.

maya: Thanks for the detailed repro steps — marking this resolved for now. If you want us to revert any prod rollouts until the agent is patched say the word. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed release perf-agent@2.0.1 to edge nodes (canary 10%). Monitoring auth errors for 15m...

julia: Can confirm the canary looks clean so far, thanks all!
